scope: Research and catalog only for an HTML/CSS/JavaScript site hosted on GitHub Pages; no site or repository modifications.

primary_sources: GitHub REST repository metadata through GitHub connector
GitHub package.json and selected README via GitHub connector
secondary_sources: MDN browser JavaScript and HTML API documentation
source_methodology.star_values: GitHub stars observed during research, not immutable counts
source_methodology.last_update_field: last_repository_push_utc from GitHub pushed_at, not latest release nor proof of active maintenance
source_methodology.npm_version_field: Version in inspected repository package manifest; not necessarily latest published npm release
source_methodology.ranking_note: Rank is an editorial fit for a lightweight GitHub Pages website, not a comparison of popularity or an independently measured audit.
source_methodology.score_scale: Editorial 1 (poor fit) to 5 (strong fit); not independently benchmarked, code-audited or user-tested.
source_methodology.null_semantics: Unverified, unavailable, not tested, or inapplicable; check surrounding field for exact meaning.

overall_recommendation.recommendation: native browser features, semantic HTML and plain CSS, with small targeted libraries only as justified

baseline.why: searchable static content, keyboard semantics and graceful degradation

baseline.technology: plain CSS with responsive media queries and custom properties

baseline.why: small payload and easy static hosting
avoid validation dependency for simple forms
browser semantics and reduced custom code

baseline.technology: image srcset, loading=lazy (offscreen), defer/module scripts, caches
Lighthouse + axe-core + ESLint + Prettier in local tooling or CI
baseline.why: quality checks are not production scripts

optional_additions_by_trigger.condition: custom accessible modal beyond native dialog

avoid_by_default: client-side router for normal multi-page navigation
polyfills unsupported by specific tested audience
overall_recommendation.preferred_hosting: GitHub Pages branch publish for unbuilt files, or GitHub Actions for static build artifacts; do not run Node server on Pages

hosting_compatibility.repo_site_base_path: Repository Pages are normally under /<repo>/; resolve assets relative to the deployed location or configure bundler base accordingly.
hosting_compatibility.root_site_base_path: User/organization Pages root sites generally use /; custom domain configurations can change routing.
hosting_compatibility.asset_paths: Test same-origin fetch, ESM MIME responses, CSS relative URLs, images, JS chunks and directly loaded nested routes.
hosting_compatibility.deploy_without_build: Commit production index.html/css/js and assets, then use Pages branch publishing; optional .nojekyll for raw output as appropriate.
hosting_compatibility.deploy_with_build: In GitHub Actions install dependencies, execute build and optional Pagefind index, then publish only generated static directory through Pages workflow.
hosting_compatibility.javascript_module_rule: Browsers need module type and valid URL imports; unresolved npm bare specifiers require import maps or bundler.
hosting_compatibility.cdn_rule: Version-pin CDN URLs, verify HTTPS, inspect license and dependencies; prefer self-hosted vendor files for control and use SRI on supported third-party classic script/style assets.
hosting_compatibility.secrets_rule: Anything shipped to HTML/CSS/JS is publicly readable; never embed private keys or privileged secrets.

native_browser_first.notes: Use DOM APIs instead of jQuery or a reactive framework for isolated interactions.
Browser provides modal focus and inert background; label dialog and include explicit close button.
Native keyboard and no-script support; ensure meaningful summary label.
Does not supply a submission backend or spam protection.
Use public or separately authenticated endpoints; do not expose API secrets.
Do not hide essential content before JavaScript successfully starts.
Do not lazy-load an above-the-fold hero/LCP image.
Favor CSS transitions where sufficient and honor reduced motion.
Bare npm imports need import maps, URL-based modules, or a bundler; use correct MIME and repository base paths.
Prefer accessible native scrolling to a heavy carousel library.

category_rankings.recommended_decision_rule: Native DOM events first; Alpine for several self-contained widgets; Stimulus for an HTML-first controller architecture.
Use native dialog/details/popover where sufficient. Consider a11y-dialog or MicroModal for custom dialogs, accordion-js for custom FAQs, focus-trap only as a low-level primitive.
Native constraint validation first. Just Validate for detailed errors. Choices or Tom Select only for genuinely complex selects.
CSS transitions and Web Animations API first; AutoAnimate for simple DOM list changes; anime.js for orchestrated timelines.
Fuse for modest public JSON indexes; Pagefind for multi-page search with a build step. Avoid running both for the same search corpus.
Chart.js for general-purpose charts; uPlot for dense time series; D3 only for unique custom graphics.
Plain image links + CSS first. PhotoSwipe for rich photo zoom, GLightbox for mixed media, Swiper only for complex carousels.
Native custom elements and CSS first; Lit for a reusable component suite; Floating UI only for challenging positioning.
Normal anchor navigation is preferred; swup for page transitions or htmx for static fragment swapping when justified.
Native lazy loading, responsive images, module defer and caching first; Quicklink only after measuring benefit; web-vitals for real-user measurement with a lawful destination.
textContent first; DOMPurify only if inserting rich untrusted HTML; Marked only for Markdown parsing, never as a sanitizer.
ESLint, Prettier, Lighthouse and axe testing locally or in CI. Vite only if bundling and build optimization become worthwhile; Pa11y for repeatable automated checks.

practical_reusable_examples.javascript:
const input = document.querySelector("#filter"); const items = [...document.querySelectorAll("#items li")];
input.addEventListener("input", () => { const q=input.value.trim().toLowerCase(); let shown=0; for(const item of items){const matched=item.textContent.toLowerCase().includes(q); item.hidden=!matched; shown+=Number(matched);} document.querySelector("#count").textContent=`${shown} results`; });
